declarations.docstring: A finite pairwise nonisomorphic family of simple group-algebra modules in the field universe has cardinality at most the number of conjugacy classes.
A finite pairwise nonisomorphic family of simple group-algebra modules in any universe has cardinality at most the number of conjugacy classes.
A linear equivalence of the modules associated with two representations induces an equivalence of those representations.
An isomorphism between the finite-dimensional representations obtained from two group-algebra modules induces a module-linear equivalence.
The group representation associated with a compatible module over the monoid algebra.
The module underlying the associated representation is linearly equivalent to the original monoid-algebra module.
The associated representation acts by the monoid-algebra element supported at the group element with coefficient one.
The algebra homomorphism of the associated representation is scalar multiplication by the monoid algebra.
A linear equivalence becomes linear over a second ring after transporting the source module structure to the target.
A module structure transported across a linear equivalence to its target.
Transporting a module structure across a base-linear equivalence preserves the compatible scalar-tower structure.
